meta.title: Mae Bio Inspirations: Slime Mold Optimization (Physarum)

chunks.title: Physarum Biology
chunks.content: Physarum polycephalum is a single-celled slime mold that solves shortest path problems. Network of tubes with protoplasmic flow. Positive feedback: tubes carrying more flow get thicker (actin-myosin stiffening). Negative feedback: unused tubes atrophy. Converges to shortest path between food sources. Recreated Tokyo rail network (Tero 2010 Science). Solves mazes, Steiner trees, multi-point optimization. Entirely distributed - no centralized processing.

chunks.title: Physarum Mathematical Model (Tero 2007)
chunks.content: Graph G=(V,E). Each edge has conductivity D_ij and flow Q_ij. Flow equation: Q_ij = (D_ij/L_ij) * (p_i - p_j). Kirchhoff conservation at nodes. Core adaptation: dD_ij/dt = f(|Q_ij|) - alpha * D_ij. f is monotonically increasing (typically |Q|^gamma, gamma>=1). First term: positive feedback (flow increases conductivity). Second term: constant decay (unused tubes shrink). Proven convergence to shortest path (Bonifaci 2012). Discretized version: O(mL(log n + log L)/epsilon^3) for (1+eps)-approximation.

chunks.title: Physarum Mae Architecture Mapping
chunks.content: Proposed PhysarumOptimizer in substrate/ module. HIGHEST PRIORITY implementation (lowest barrier, highest value). MycelialSubstrate connections = tubes. Message traffic = protoplasmic flow. Connection bandwidth = conductivity D_ij. Per-step update: new_conductivity = conductivity + dt*(f(traffic) - alpha*conductivity). Current static topologies (ring, mesh, scale-free, small-world) become initial conditions. Integrates with MycelialSubstrate (direct), NutrientFlow (preferential flow), GNNCommunicator (adaptive topology), CircadianRhythm (aggressive optimization during REST), EventBus (traffic metrics). Novel: self-optimizing infrastructure without central planner.
